decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording both selection of the orientation that produces the cleanest connector layout and adaptation of the enclosure to that orientation.
The source concerns orientation of the integrated board and adaptation of its case; it does not change the independently specified mechanical layout of the earlier modular power board.
Allowing the integrated board orientation to follow the cleanest overall connector layout does not alter the modular power board battery-connector placement or clearance rules.
The source applies to the integrated board under current discussion and does not revise the separate modular main board's rail orientation, dimensions, or connector-placement constraints.
The integrated-board orientation decision does not change the separate sensor board's established vertical mounting and connector-access requirements.
The source changes enclosure dependence on integrated-board orientation but does not change the panel-mounted button, its connector, signal connection, or control behavior.
Connector-layout orientation for the integrated board does not alter the historical modular interboard topology, connector types, or pinouts.
The board-orientation and enclosure decision has no necessary effect on the task-local manufacturer ordering assistance requirement.
Mechanical orientation and case adaptation do not change the AXP2101 electrical power-path or simultaneous charging requirements.
Choosing board orientation by connector-layout cleanliness does not revise component sourceability, cost, or JLCPCB Basic-part policies.
The source does not alter the sensor board's connector inventory, module interfaces, pin assignments, or connector count.
The mechanical orientation decision does not change I2C cable length, speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor configuration.
